title: Introduce asynchronous tiered autoscaler and decoupled reservation reservoir
author: Asha Patel
description:
Motivation: Dedicated fleets see sudden, short-lived tenant spikes that existing synchronous autoscalers either overprovision for or respond too slowly. This PR introduces a new asynchronous, tiered autoscaler that separates long-running reservation decisions from short-term burst smoothing. It decouples the reservation ledger into a lightweight in-memory reservoir that can be tuned independently of the backing persistent commitments, reducing lock contention and improving decision latency.

What this PR does: Adds an AsyncTieredAutoscaler controller that runs two independent decision loops: (1) a slow, commitment allocator that manages backing reservations (commit window sizing, graceful decommit) and (2) a fast reservoir reconciler which issues ephemeral burst credits from a local in-memory pool. The reservoir uses a leaky-bucket estimator augmented with a time-weighted utilization drift reporter to smooth microbursts while preserving per-tenant throughput guarantees.

Key features and rationale: - Decoupled reservation reservoir: local, lock-free allocation to satisfy short bursts without writing to the central ledger for every microburst. Backing reservations are reconciled asynchronously to reduce high-frequency contention. - Tiered decision loops: slow loop handles policy-driven commitments and safety windows; fast loop serves immediate capacity requests and enforces short-term fairness. - Throughput guarantees: per-tenant SLA enforcement remains anchored to the backing commitments. The reservoir grants are conservative and honor minimum throughput floors. - Burst smoothing: leaky-bucket + exponential decay estimator reduces noisy oscillations when many tenants spike simultaneously. - Utilization telemetry exporter: new metrics for reservoir_fill_ratio, reservoir_drain_rate, drifted_utilization_percentile and commit_reconcile_lag to help SREs tune policies. - Fallback semantics: when the reservoir is exhausted, requests fall back to the legacy AdmissionController path which applies existing throttles and queued admission. This preserves graceful degradation. - Configuration: introduces a new AutoscalerPolicy CRD fields (asyncReservoirEnabled, reservoirSizeFraction, fastLoopIntervalMs, slowLoopIntervalSec, driftDecayAlpha) with sane defaults and per-tenant overrides.

Migration notes: Existing clusters will continue using the legacy synchronous autoscaler by default. Enabling the async tiered autoscaler is a feature-flagged rollout. We provide a migration tool (scripts/migration/commit-to-reservoir.sh) that safely seeds reservoirs from current commitments for canary pools.

Testing and validation: Unit tests for reservoir accounting and fast-loop invariants, integration tests in perf-canary harness simulating 1k tenants with randomized burst patterns, and cluster soak test on staging for 72 hours. Load tests show 32% reduction in commit-write rate under microburst workload and 12% lower 95th percentile tail latency for admission decisions.

Related: builds on earlier work for warm pools and tokenized burst banking but follows a different approach by avoiding synchronous ledger writes on microbursts. References: Linear ENG-4219, SUP-1132 (support incident that motivated quick response path).

release_notes: Introduce Async Tiered Autoscaler (opt-in). Adds per-pool in-memory reservoir for burst smoothing, new AutoscalerPolicy fields, and several reservoir/commit telemetry metrics. Defaults keep legacy autoscaler behavior unless enabled. See docs/autoscaler/async-tiered-design.md for tuning guidance.
tests: Unit: 84 tests covering allocator invariants and accounting. Integration: perf-canary scenario with 1k tenants and stochastic bursts (72h soak). notes_for_sre: New metrics to watch: autoscaler_reservoir_fill_ratio{pool}, autoscaler_reservoir_drain_rate{pool}, autoscaler_commit_reconcile_lag_seconds. If reconcile_lag grows >5s, reduce reservoirSizeFraction or increase slowLoopIntervalSec. Grafana dashboard draft is in docs/.
